title: CVA scan profile
description: Two orthogonal axes in ONE schema, not eight files (§5.6, resolving C11). The four POLICY profiles (baseline/strict/blackbox/selftest) each declare a default BUDGET tier (triage/standard/deep/forensic), and any tier is selectable against any policy via --budget-tier. Unknown keys are a LOAD ERROR, not a warning: a profile with a typo'd threshold silently runs at the default, and the operator believes they tightened something they did not.
$comment: unevaluatedProperties, NOT additionalProperties. The latter is evaluated against sibling `properties` only and DOES NOT COMPOSE under allOf/oneOf — which is exactly how a base schema plus four variants wants to be written. Getting it wrong fails in the flattering direction: the baseline validates, the strict variant does not, and the obvious 'fix' is to delete the constraint.

budget_tier.description: The second axis. A check excluded here reports UNAVAILABLE with exclusion_reason='budget' and an estimated cost — NOT a fifth Availability state (§5.5). Cost-awareness lands in the schema at B1 even though profiles land at B6, because retrofitting it after detectors exist means touching every one of them.

checks.description: null = every registered check. An explicit list is how a budget tier excludes; the excluded checks still appear in the plan and the coverage statement, stating why.

disabled_checks.description: The blackbox policy's mechanism: white-box detectors disabled UP FRONT, so the report says 'not asked to' rather than 'could not' — two different facts about the scan.

cost_ceiling_s.description: Derived from the MEASURED CPU throughput at B4, never from backend_revised §3.6's ~20 img/s figure: that is a 6 GB GPU number and no GPU exists in this project (§4.3, R6).

egress_guard.description: selftest arms pytest-socket programmatically. It must be called as a LIBRARY, not via pytest's --disable-socket flag: cva selftest is a product entry point, and relying on the flag means the guard is armed in CI and absent in the shipped binary — the deployment that matters.

pin_clock.description: selftest only. With scan_id derived from --seed, this is what makes V10's diff EMPTY rather than merely small.

thresholds.description: No constant lives in code — every threshold comes from here, so a tuning change never requires a code change and the profile hash records exactly what was applied.

detector_options.description: Per-detector options, keyed by detector_id. This is the ONE mechanism by which a plug-in receives profile settings — §7.5's check() signature has no slot for them, and leaving each family to invent its own would put three different answers in three packages.

evidence.description: Evidence caps live in the profile so the <25 MB single-file HTML target is an EVIDENCE-COUNT BUDGET decided in advance, not something discovered on demo day. Base64 inflates 4/3.

psi.description: Backend does not implement PSI, but the profile must carry what the CORRECTED null needs: PSI ~ (1/N + 1/M)·chi2(B-1). The scale factor is the entire content of the published result (Post-Merge R1), and both sample sizes appear in the critical value.

group_key.description: PARAMETERISED, per PS audit G2: PS §2.2.1 names three levels — 'contributor, batch or source metadata' — and hard-coding one silently drops the other two.

disposition.description: The policy is ONE FILE an organisation can change without touching code. Whichever rule fired is written into Finding.disposition_rule.

rules.description: ORDER IS SEMANTIC and two constraints are easy to get wrong. D2 must sit ABOVE D3, or a benign conversion matches D3 first. And D1 must be SCOPED TO prov.* — a model.weight_digest mismatch is also a deterministic failure, so an unscoped D1 would swallow every substitution finding before D2 ever runs, quietly restoring the exact false alarm D2 exists to prevent.

attack_class.description: D2 keys on attack_class == 'benign_conversion', NOT on a tolerance predicate: the tolerance band is DETECTOR-INTERNAL and the risk engine sees Findings, not fingerprints.

min_severity.description: D1's and D5's floors are load-bearing. prov.* bypass calibration and arrive at confidence 1.0, so an unfloored D1 quarantines boundary_flip, degraded_gap and clock_regression — reintroducing the exact false alarm that boundary_flip was approved to remove.

cap.description: D6: drift-vs-manipulation is CAPPED at review, never quarantine alone.

exclude_detector_prefixes.description: prov.* — a hash mismatch is arithmetic, not a belief.

determinism.$comment: CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG is GPU-OVERLAY ONLY and has no place in a CPU profile.
